title: epoll_event structure
summary: An epoll_event is the structure used with epoll_ctl(2) and epoll_wait(2). It contains an events bitmask (EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLERR, EPOLLHUP, EPOLLET, EPOLLONESHOT, ...) and a 64-bit user data field (usually a pointer or fd).

ext.summary: An epoll_event is the structure used with epoll_ctl(2) and epoll_wait(2). It contains an events bitmask (EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLERR, EPOLLHUP, EPOLLET, EPOLLONESHOT, ...) and a 64-bit user data field (usually a pointer or fd).

structure.meaning: Event bitmask: EPOLLIN (0x001), EPOLLOUT (0x004), EPOLLERR (0x008), EPOLLHUP (0x010), EPOLLRDHUP (0x2000), EPOLLET (0x80000000, edge-triggered), EPOLLONESHOT (0x40000000), EPOLLWAKEUP (0x20000000).
User data: pointer, fd, u32, or u64. Echoed back in epoll_wait results.

notes: epoll is Linux's scalable I/O event notification (O(n) setup, O(1) wait).
Level-triggered (default) vs edge-triggered (EPOLLET): edge-triggered requires draining the fd.
EPOLLONESHOT disables the fd after one event; re-arm with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
epoll is the basis of high-performance servers (nginx, Redis, Node.js libuv on Linux).
